title: Integrated Whispering-Gallery Microlaser-Waveguide Platform for On-Chip Electrical Excitation of InGaAs Quantum Dots
authors: Léo J. Roche, Peter Gschwandtner, Chirag C. Palekar, Setthanat Wijitpatima, Yuhui Yang, Monika Emmerling, Sven Höfling, Tobias Huber-Loyola, Stephan Reitzenstein
abstract: We report the fabrication and characterization of an integrated quantum photonic device consisting of an electrically driven whispering-gallery-mode micropillar laser evanescently coupled to a ridge waveguide, both incorporating InGaAs quantum dots (QDs). The lasing characteristics of microlasers are systematically investigated as a function of the pillar-waveguide gap distance. Coherent emission from the whispering-gallery-mode microlaser coupled into the waveguide enables on-chip optical excitation of QDs embedded in an electrically contacted micropillar at the end of the waveguide. Under continuous-wave on-chip excitation, we observe single-photon emission with $g^{(2)}(0) = (3.49 \pm 0.01) \%$ for a QD integrated in the outcoupling micropillar which can be spectrally tuned-by the quantum confined Stark effect. These results constitute an important step toward low-footprint, deterministic, and scalable single-photon sources for QD-based integrated quantum photonic circuits.
summary: The research reports on an integrated platform combining a Whispering-Gallery Microlaser with a waveguide to electrically excite InGaAs Quantum Dots. By systematically characterizing the laser coupling and performing Hanbury Brown and Twiss measurements, the authors demonstrate high-purity single-photon emission necessary for scalable quantum photonic circuits.
main_problem: The goal is to develop a low-footprint, deterministic, and scalable integrated quantum photonic circuit capable of generating single photons on demand.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated high-purity single-photon emission ($g^{(2)}(0) = 3.49 \pm 0.01\%$) by coupling light from an electrically driven Whispering-Gallery Microlaser into a waveguide to excite embedded InGaAs Quantum Dots.
method: The study combines electrical characterization of the microlaser (IV curves, threshold analysis) with optical measurements, including Hanbury Brown and Twiss (HBT) correlation measurements on the QD emission.
model_or_system: The physical system is an integrated quantum photonic circuit featuring a WGM micropillaser coupled evanescently to a ridge waveguide, which in turn excites InGaAs Quantum Dots embedded in a Waveguide Interconnect Module (WIM). The QDs are electrically tunable via the quantum-confined Stark effect.
key_observables: Second-order correlation function $g^{(2)}(0)$, single-photon emission rate, lasing threshold current ($I_{th}$), and spectral tuning range ($\le 0.35 	ext{ nm}$).
important_parameters: Gap distance ($d_{gap}$), injection current (up to 1 mA), and the ratio $\eta_{WGM} = I_{WGM}/I_{tot}$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the measured $g^{(2)}(0)$ value confirms single-photon purity, and power dependence fitting suggests the presence of exciton (X) or biexciton (XX) states.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate device architecture, $d_{gap}$-dependent lasing characteristics (thresholds/Q-factors), spectral comparisons between on-chip vs. off-chip excitation, and current dependence analysis for QD emission lines.
paper_structure: The paper systematically characterizes the WGM microlaser performance as a function of coupling gap distance ($d_{gap}$), establishes the mechanism of light transfer from the laser to the waveguide, and finally demonstrates single-photon generation via HBT measurements on the excited QDs.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the integration challenge in quantum photonics by merging high-quality cavity sources (WGM lasers) with solid-state emitters (QDs) onto a chip, which is crucial for building scalable quantum networks and computing modules.
